title: Call Smarter, Not More
hook: A two-layer model that cuts a 40,000-customer call list to 8,589 and raises conversion from 7.2% to 31.7%

slides.title: Call Smarter, Not More
slides.subtitle: A two-layer calling model for a term deposit marketing campaign
slides.narration: A bank wants to sell term deposits by phone, but most people say no. Divyesh built a system that works out who is actually worth calling.

slides.title: The problem
bullets: 40,000 customers on the marketing list, and only 2,896 (7.2%) subscribed
Calling everyone wastes hours on people who were never going to say yes
Calling too few misses real subscribers
The goal: keep almost every real subscriber while removing as many wasted calls as possible
slides.narration: Fewer than one in thirteen customers said yes. The challenge was to cut the wasted calls without losing the people who would have subscribed.

slides.title: A funnel, not a single model

steps.label: Screen
steps.detail: Layer 1 uses only information known before any contact to remove obvious no's cheaply

steps.label: Refine
steps.detail: Layer 2 adds contact history (campaign contacts, call duration) to sharpen the list

steps.label: Prioritise
steps.detail: Clustering splits the final list into segments, so the best ones get called first

slides.narration: Rather than one big model, he built a funnel. Each stage only uses information that would actually be available at that point in a real campaign.

slides.title: Layer 1: Cold screening
bullets: Logistic Regression + CatBoost, blended by a meta-learner trained on 5-fold out-of-fold predictions
Only 7 pre-contact features: day, month, contact channel, age, marital status, balance, housing
Full list: 40,000 → 30,777 customers, losing only 113 real subscribers (3.9%)
slides.narration: With only basic customer details, the first layer removed over nine thousand calls that would have been wasted. That's about 560 hours of calling time, or 70 working days.

slides.title: Layer 2: Informed refinement
bullets: XGBoost on Layer 1's 30,777 customers, with 13 features including campaign contacts and call duration
Threshold 0.28: the highest recall that keeps precision at or above 30%
Removed 78% of the remaining wasted calls on the test set, missing 21 of 557 subscribers
Final list: 30,777 → 8,589 customers
slides.narration: Once contact history is available, the second layer becomes far more accurate. It removed almost four out of five remaining wasted calls and still kept 96 percent of subscribers.

slides.title: The funnel, end to end
slides.unit: Conversion rate of the call list (%)

metrics.label: Real subscribers still on the list

slides.narration: Overall, the call list went from about one yes in fourteen to nearly one in three, while still holding on to 94 percent of every real subscriber.

slides.title: Who to call first
bullets: UMAP + Ward hierarchical clustering on the final 8,589 customers, k = 2–10 scanned
Best silhouette score: 0.699 at k = 10
Segments with 150+ customers cover 98.7% of the list
slides.narration: Even within the final list, some groups convert much better than others. Calling the strongest segments first gets more subscribers from the same number of calls.

slides.title: Limitations
bullets: The original goal of 80% yes-recall and 50% no-recall at the same time was not reachable at any threshold, so the chosen threshold is a compromise
Call duration is the strongest Layer 2 feature, but it's only known after a call, so Layer 2 suits follow-up rounds rather than first contact
Pool-level numbers include training rows, so the test-set numbers are the fair benchmark
The best k was at the edge of the scanned range, so the 10 segments are a starting point
slides.narration: He's upfront about the limits. The original targets turned out to be impossible to hit together, and the second layer relies on information you only get after a call.

slides.title: What's next, and explore it yourself
bullets: Next: widen the clustering scan to k = 15–20 to confirm the right number of segments
Built a companion Power BI dashboard that shows the payoff in hours and working days saved
Biggest lesson: decide which features are fair to use at each stage before building the model
All three notebooks are on GitHub
slides.narration: The notebooks are all on GitHub. The biggest lesson was to think about when each piece of information is actually available before modelling with it.
